enriched_description: Fleet equine mammal measuring 120-150 cm at withers with distinctive black-and-white striped coat pattern. Stripes unique to each individual, extending across body, legs, and mane. Head elongated with large dark eyes and mobile ears. Neck arched with erect bristly mane. Body robust and muscular. Legs long and slender terminating in single dark hooves. Tail long with black tufted hair. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse body hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. African equine with herd behavior. Stripes serve as camouflage and fly deterrent.

Domestic swine measuring 90-180 cm body length weighing 50-350 kg. Body stocky and barrel-shaped with sparse coarse bristles over pink, black, or spotted skin. Head large with elongated snout ending in cartilaginous disk for rooting. Eyes small. Ears large and floppy or erect depending on breed. Legs short and stout with cloven hooves. Tail short and curly. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Omnivorous with highly developed olfactory sense.

Wild swine measuring 90-180 cm body length weighing 50-200 kg. Body robust with coarse dark brown to black bristly fur over thick skin. Head large with prominent elongated snout. Males possess prominent curved tusks (enlarged canines) protruding from mouth. Eyes small and dark. Ears pointed and erect. Legs sturdy with cloven hooves. Tail short and straight. Dorsal ridge of stiff bristles forming mane. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, hair insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Narrower body than domestic pig with prominent tusks.

African wild swine measuring 90-150 cm body length weighing 50-150 kg. Body laterally compressed with sparse coarse gray-brown bristles. Head large and flattened with distinctive warty protuberances on face (orbital and maxillary warts). Prominent curved tusks protruding upward from lower jaw and outward from upper jaw. Snout broad and flat. Eyes high-set on head. Ears large and pointed. Legs relatively long for a suid. Tail long and thin with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

Massive semiaquatic mammal measuring 3-5 m body length weighing 1500-3200 kg. Body barrel-shaped with thick nearly hairless skin in gray-brown coloration. Skin secretes reddish oily substance acting as sunscreen. Head enormous comprising one-third of body length with broad muzzle. Eyes, ears, and nostrils positioned on top of head for semiaquatic lifestyle. Mouth extremely wide with large tusk-like canines and incisors. Legs short and stubby with four webbed toes. Tail short and flattened. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

Adult castrated bovine measuring 140-180 cm at withers weighing 400-900 kg. Body massive and muscular with short dense coat in white, brown, black, or pied coloration. Head broad with wide muzzle. Horns curved laterally and upward (if not dehorned). Eyes large and dark with wide field of vision. Ears large and mobile. Neck thick and muscular with prominent dewlap. Body deep-chested with strong back. Legs sturdy with cloven hooves. Tail long with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, hair insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

Large Asian bovine measuring 150-190 cm at withers weighing 300-1200 kg. Body massive with sparse dark gray to black hair over thick skin. Head elongated with broad forehead. Horns massive, laterally curved, and triangular in cross-section measuring up to 2 m span. Eyes dark. Ears relatively small. Neck short and thick. Body deep and barrel-shaped. Legs sturdy with broad cloven hooves adapted for wet terrain. Tail long with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Often domesticated as draft animal.

Large bovid measuring 160-200 cm at withers weighing 350-1000 kg. Body massive with shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump. Head large and broad with short curved horns. Beard of long hair on chin and throat. Eyes dark. Ears small and hidden in fur. Hindquarters less heavily furred. Legs sturdy with cloven hooves. Tail short with bushy tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, dense fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Short horns compared to body size. Herd-dwelling grazer.

Uncastrated adult male sheep measuring 65-110 cm at withers weighing 35-180 kg. Body covered with dense woolly fleece in white, brown, or black. Head broad with laterally spiraling horns (in horned breeds). Horns thick and ridged. Eyes dark with horizontal rectangular pupils. Ears lateral and drooping. Neck thick and muscular. Body compact and stocky. Legs sturdy with cloven hooves. Tail short. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, wool insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Secondary sexual characteristics include larger size and prominent horns.

Wild sheep measuring 80-110 cm at withers weighing 50-140 kg. Body covered with short brown to gray-brown coat with white rump patch. Males possess massive tightly curled horns weighing up to 14 kg with annual growth rings. Horns curve laterally then downward and backward. Head broad with large dark eyes. Ears short and pointed. Body muscular and agile adapted for mountainous terrain. Legs sturdy with specialized hooves providing traction on rocky surfaces. Tail short. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.
